- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid missing downward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: reduce forecast slope by 50% after sentiment drop.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- In low-sentiment periods (sentiment <0.33 for 3+ days), model underperforms; add 0.5–1.5% bias upward to counteract pessimism.
- If forecast is consistently below true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, model is underestimating; increase forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- Sentiment history with alternating 0.33/1.00 patterns suggests model is overfitting to short-term noise; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast.
